lead.project: Save a copy someone else can import into Fabricator.

format.label: Export it as
format.projectDesc: To keep building it in Fabricator · .fabricator
format.appDesc: To use it, in a window of its own · .rayfin

code.desc: Source and settings. Installed packages and build output stay out.

app.desc: It opens in a window of its own, with this name and icon. Its data stays on the computer it’s installed on.

history.desc: Every saved version, so History and Restore work for them too.

published.include: Their publishes update this same app. They’ll need access to its workspace.
published.exclude: They’ll publish it as a new app, in a workspace they choose.

never.project: Never included: your chat, secret values, local app data or sign-ins.
never.projectSecrets: Never included: your chat, secret values ({{secrets}}), local app data or sign-ins.
never.app: Never included: your chat, version history, where it’s published, secret values, local app data or sign-ins.
never.appSecrets: Never included: your chat, version history, where it’s published, secret values ({{secrets}}), local app data or sign-ins.

export.keptOut: Also left out in case they hold secrets: {{files}}.
export.secretsWarning: It uses secrets that don’t come with it, so what needs them won’t work where it’s installed.

next.title: What happens next
next.send: Send them the file, by email, chat or a shared folder.
next.openApp: They double-click it. Fabricator asks before it installs the app, then opens it in a window of its own. The first time takes a minute or two. Don’t have Fabricator?
next.openProject: They double-click it to import it into Fabricator, or select Open existing, then Import a project. New to Fabricator?
next.afterApp: After that it opens like any app. On Windows it’s in the Start menu, under Rayfin apps.
next.access: So they can publish, give them Contributor access to {{workspace}} in Fabric.
